title: Dessert Recipe Roundup
contentHtml:
Are you team apple, pumpkin, pecan, or all of the above when it comes to Thanksgiving pies? Turns out, we might just be team apple.

Pie: Some people love it, some people hate it, and some people are entirely indifferent to it until the fourth Thursday in November. No matter where your love–hate relationship with the Thanksgiving staple lies, we have some recipes that are worth a try. Dive into the roundup below!

This is one Warm & Koji dessert!

Pie Crusts & Apple Fillings

One of my earliest viral recipes was a vodka pie crust recipe I developed back at Cook's Illustrated magazine way back in 2006. The key here is a good food processor, keeping things contained and consistent: Cook's Illustrated's Foolproof Pie Dough. 🔗

This version takes the food processor method a step further; rather than leaving butter in discrete “pea-sized pieces,” you take the butter and half the flour and blend it into a paste before pulsing the remaining flour in with a food processor. The result is a foolproof dough that's easy to work with and bakes up beautifully: Easy Pie Dough. 🔗

Apple pie is as American as, well, apple pie! This recipe keeps it classic but offers some fun variations to try, including one resembling an apple crumble and one that adds a layer of nutty aged cheese, like cheddar: Perfect Apple Pie. 🔗

For a gooier apple pie filling, your sous vide might just have the answers. In fact, regardless of the recipe you go with, parcooking the apples is always a good idea—you can use a dutch oven or sous vide—to help the apples retain their shape and flavor as they bake: Gooey Apple Pie. 🔗

And finally, we'd be remiss if we left out the newest apple dessert recipe. Following our "Warm & Koji" theme, this Miso Caramel Apple Tarte Tatin brings a savory complexity to the buttery, flaky, sweetness of caramel—and it goes beautifully with this koji-fermented whipped cream: Miso Caramel Apple Tarte Tatin. 🔗

[Image Credit: Vicky Wasik, Serious Eats]

Pumpkins, Pecans, and Other Pies

If you didn't notice throughout the section above, apples are a sweet spot for JKLA World HQ. That is to say... we almost exclusively focus on making and sharing apple desserts. Oops! Though there's also this late summer Caramelized Plum Cornbread Cake if you want to take a shot at a winter stone fruit dessert.

If you're looking for a pecan or pumpkin pie recipe, though, here are some options from some Serious Eats colleagues:

  • As Stella Parks says, "butternut squash may not evoke the romance of a jack o' lantern or Cinderella's carriage, but it has all the earthy flavor of a pumpkin at a fraction of the hassle" in this Butternut Pumpkin Pie recipe. 🔗

  • Similarly, this sweet potato pie—also by Stella Parks—brings the flavor that canned purée might just be missing. See for yourself: Silky Sweet Potato Pie Recipe. 🔗

  • For some Americans, including Lauren Weisenthal, pecan pie is a non-negotiable on their Thanksgiving table. This recipe is sweet in all the right ways: Classic Pecan Pie Recipe. 🔗

  • Or how about a chiffon pie, by Arlyn Osborne, that takes the classic flavors of pumpkin pie and makes them light and airy with the help of a Swiss meringue: Pumpkin Chiffon Pie. 🔗
